market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate: Banks Face Implementation Deadline
market.summary_short: European banks are racing to implement the EU's Instant Payments Regulation, with a critical deadline approaching for receiving instant credit transfers. The regulation aims to make instant payments universally available, affordable, and secure across the Eurozone.
market.summary_detail: The EU Instant Payments Regulation mandates that all payment service providers (PSPs) in the Eurozone must be able to receive instant credit transfers by early 2025, with sending capabilities following shortly after. This regulation also introduces caps on instant payment fees, ensuring they are no higher than standard SEPA credit transfer fees. Furthermore, PSPs must offer a "Verification of Payee" (VoP) service to combat fraud, a significant new requirement. The regulation's phased rollout presents challenges for banks, particularly those in CEE, requiring substantial upgrades to their payment infrastructure and compliance systems. Corporates will benefit from faster liquidity management and real-time transaction visibility.
key_points: Mandatory instant payment receipt by early 2025 for Eurozone PSPs.
Instant payment fees capped at standard SEPA credit transfer rates.
"Verification of Payee" (VoP) service becomes mandatory for fraud prevention.
Regulation aims for universal, affordable, and secure instant payments across the EU.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is highly critical for RBI Cash Management and CMIplus. It necessitates immediate upgrades to ensure full compliance with instant payment processing and the new VoP requirements across all CEE network banks. CMIplus must support these capabilities to remain competitive and offer seamless, compliant instant payment services to its corporate clients.

market.title: PSD3 Proposals Advance Open Banking for Corporate Treasury
market.summary_short: The European Commission's proposals for PSD3 and the new Payment Services Regulation (PSR) aim to strengthen consumer protection and further develop open banking. These changes will significantly impact corporate treasury by enabling more sophisticated API-driven services.
market.summary_detail: PSD3 and the PSR are set to replace PSD2, addressing its shortcomings and expanding the scope of open banking. Key proposals include enhanced fraud prevention measures, improved data sharing mechanisms, and clearer rules for third-party providers (TPPs). For corporate treasury, this means greater potential for real-time cash management, automated reconciliation, and potentially eBAM (electronic Bank Account Management) through standardized APIs. Banks will need to invest further in robust API infrastructure and security protocols to support these advanced services, fostering a more integrated and efficient financial ecosystem across Europe. The focus on API standardization will be crucial for multi-bank connectivity.
key_points: PSD3 and PSR replace PSD2, focusing on fraud and open banking expansion.
Enhanced data sharing and clearer rules for Third-Party Providers (TPPs).
Potential for advanced corporate treasury services via APIs, including eBAM.
Banks require further investment in secure and standardized API infrastructure.

market.title: AI Revolutionizes Payment Fraud Prevention Amidst Real-Time Threats
market.summary_short: With the surge in instant payments, financial institutions and corporates are increasingly deploying Artificial Intelligence (AI) to detect and prevent sophisticated payment fraud. AI-driven solutions offer real-time anomaly detection, significantly enhancing security measures.
market.summary_detail: The rapid adoption of instant payments, while beneficial for liquidity, also presents new challenges for fraud prevention, as fraudulent transactions can clear almost immediately. AI and machine learning algorithms are proving indispensable in this fight, analyzing vast datasets of transaction patterns, user behavior, and network anomalies in real-time. These systems can identify suspicious activities that human analysts might miss, such as unusual payment amounts, unfamiliar beneficiaries, or deviations from typical corporate spending profiles. Implementing AI requires robust data governance and integration with existing treasury and payment systems, but the investment yields substantial returns in reducing financial losses and maintaining trust.

Real-time anomaly detection identifies suspicious transaction patterns.

market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate Accelerates CEE Adoption
market.summary_short: New EU regulation mandates instant payment availability and caps fees, significantly impacting CEE banks and corporates. This accelerates the shift from traditional payment methods, requiring system upgrades.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's new Instant Payments Regulation, effective early 2026, requires all payment service providers (PSPs) in the EU and EEA to offer instant credit transfers in EUR within 10 seconds, 24/7, 365 days a year. Crucially, it also mandates that charges for instant payments cannot exceed those for standard credit transfers. This regulation is a game-changer for the CEE region, where instant payment adoption has been varied. Banks must now ensure their infrastructure supports real-time processing and robust fraud prevention for these high-speed transactions. Corporates will benefit from improved liquidity management and faster cash flow, but also face the challenge of integrating real-time capabilities into their treasury systems. The regulation aims to boost the EU's strategic autonomy and reduce reliance on foreign payment schemes.

Fees capped at standard credit transfer rates.
Effective early 2026 for EU/EEA PSPs.
Significant impact on CEE banking infrastructure and corporate liquidity.

For CEE banks, aligning with these global standards is crucial for seamless cross-border operations and maintaining competitiveness. The transition also presents an opportunity to streamline internal processes and leverage the enhanced data for better treasury insights.

market.title: Open Banking APIs Transform Corporate Treasury Operations
market.summary_short: Open Banking APIs are increasingly adopted by corporates to gain real-time visibility and control over cash across multiple banks. This technology enhances liquidity management and automates treasury processes.
market.summary_detail: The expansion of Open Banking beyond retail banking is significantly impacting corporate treasury, particularly through the adoption of APIs for real-time data exchange. Corporates are leveraging these APIs to connect directly with various bank accounts, gaining consolidated views of balances and transactions across their multi-bank relationships. This real-time visibility is crucial for effective liquidity management, cash forecasting, and optimizing working capital. While security and standardization remain key considerations, the benefits in terms of efficiency and control are driving rapid adoption, especially among large international corporates operating in diverse regions like CEE.

market.title: ECB Launches Pontes for Tokenised Wholesale Settlement
market.summary_short: The European Central Bank has introduced Pontes, a new solution designed to facilitate wholesale transactions in tokenised assets. This initiative allows for the settlement of these transactions using central bank money.
market.summary_detail: The Eurosystem, comprising the ECB and national central banks of the Eurozone, has launched Pontes, a significant step towards integrating tokenised finance into the traditional financial system. Pontes provides a mechanism for wholesale transactions involving tokenised assets to be settled directly in central bank money, aiming to enhance efficiency and reduce settlement risk. This move signals the ECB's commitment to exploring the potential of distributed ledger technology (DLT) for financial markets, potentially paving the way for future innovations in securities and payments. It's a crucial development for the evolution of digital finance infrastructure within the Eurozone, impacting how large corporates might manage liquidity and assets in the future.

regulatory.title: EBA Fraud Taxonomy 7.0 Released, Effective January 2027 for PSR Compliance
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA released version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, effective January 1, 2027, to harmonise fraud reporting and support the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation. It includes updates for latest fraud trends like emotional manipulation and suspected money mule activity.
regulatory.summary_detail: On June 3, 2026, the Euro Banking Association published version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, which will become effective on January 1, 2027. This annual review ensures the taxonomy remains relevant to evolving fraud trends, with updates developed by the Expert Group on Payment Fraud-related Topics (EGPF). Key changes in version 7.0 include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with more specific modi like 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', and 'charity / donation fraud'. Additionally, new labels for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud have been added. The taxonomy provides a harmonised pan-European framework for classifying payment fraud scenarios, improving data comparability, monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, particularly in anticipation of the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation.
key_points: Version 7.0 effective date: January 1, 2027.
Updates reflect latest fraud trends and improve categorisation.
Supports harmonised fraud data sharing under forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR).
New modi for emotional manipulation fraud and tags for money mule/card chip relay.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI CMIplus needs to ensure its fraud monitoring and reporting systems are updated to align with EBA Fraud Taxonomy version 7.0 by January 1, 2027. This is crucial for compliance with the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation's information-sharing requirements.
